effect: The harshest AI occupiers can now choose to expel the resident population, exceedingly rarely (design decision, 2026-11-18: ethnic relocation and cleansing in harsher situations is a reality; the game should reflect it for the most unconstrained regimes, exceedingly rarely). Before, the AI never chose its 'displacement' occupation policy: it picks the cheapest of administration, repression and displacement (PTo), and displacement can never be cheapest (its troop-loss estimate, 0.041 x hostility per million residents, is above repression's 0.0275 x hostility before any weight, and expelled people add 2.5 x the restraint weight, which is at least 0.072). Now, before that comparison, an AI occupier picks displacement when all of these hold: its regime is among the most unconstrained in the game (the game's own constraint score C1 at most 0.15: one-party states, absolute monarchies and juntas with a single-party legislature; every democracy and hybrid regime template scores about 0.3 or more), no sanctions coalition has formed against it (the GDP of every country taking part in any active sanctions regime against it, whatever the cause: aggression, a UN resolution, atrocities or a manual coalition, below 5 % of world GDP, summed as the game's own d1r does for atrocity sanctions), its leader is among the most brutal (brutality trait 0.75 or more: 11 of the 263 seeded leaders), and the population it occupies is in open hostility (population-weighted mean occupation hostility 0.75 or more, the game's own uprising threshold). When any condition lapses it returns to the game's cost comparison. The expulsion itself is the game's existing policy: a share of each province's residents leaves each month, harm, deaths and the war-conduct record follow the game's rules, and the conduct and sanction mechanics react as they already do. Real-world behaviour: mass expulsion of occupied populations is rare and comes from unaccountable regimes in wars where the population is treated as hostile (Nagorno-Karabakh 2023, the 1990s Balkan wars, Darfur), not from every authoritarian occupier. Expected frequency: very rare, because it needs all four conditions at once: the regime condition admits only the three authoritarian regime types with a single-party legislature, the leader condition about 4 % of seeded leaders, and both must coincide with an occupation in open hostility and no sanctions against the occupier (estimated from the seeded regime templates and traits; not measured in a run). Deterministic: only regime, sanction, trait and province state; no random draw. Day 0 unchanged; no new state. AI countries only; the player's choice is unchanged. Minified names are those of build 26734764.
